headline: Software engineer attempts to troubleshoot BRICS AI by emailing prompt to local neighborhood grocery store owner
body:
Q: Rajesh, you recently claimed you successfully 'debugged' the proposed BRICS open-source AI zone. How exactly did you achieve this?

A: It was straightforward. Since the AI is meant to be an open-source collaborative effort, I assumed it functioned like a community cooperative. I didn't want to deal with complex Git repositories, so I just wrote my primary algorithm on a piece of cardboard and dropped it off at the local kirana store where the uncle in charge handles all our neighborhood’s logistical 'infrastructure'.

Q: And did he understand the implications of cross-continental machine learning datasets?

A: He didn't even blink. He looked at my logic gates, asked if they were gluten-free, and then placed them between a sack of basmati rice and a stack of newspapers. He told me the 'data flow' would be optimized by morning because the local stray cat usually sleeps on that specific pile, and cats are known for their high-frequency vibration processors.

Q: What was the outcome of this international technological integration?

A: Remarkably, my AI started outputting perfect grocery inventory lists instead of global economic policy. It’s significantly more accurate than the prototype, and frankly, I think the store owner’s method of manual packet-switching by courier-boy is the future of decentralized tech.
caption: BRICS AI initiative takes a local turn as neighborhood grocery store replaces cloud computing with a pile of rice sacks. Tech giants are reportedly furious. #BRICS #AI #Innovation #TechNews (satire)
